summary: A first-person excerpt from a novel's Book 3 describes the narrator's lingering trauma after returning from Baalum in the Peten, with Sarah drifting and then recovering, Lou hovering over her, and David submitting a rough cut of Baby Love to Sundance. The narrator, working late at Applecore on re-cut interviews to replace those of Carly and Paula, is set to face the final act of the story involving Alex Goddard, who believes he is Shiva. The passage ends mid-sentence as the narrator decides to stop working.
one_line: Narrator's aftermath of the Baalum ordeal, Sarah's recovery, and the Baby Love project, leading to Alex Goddard's final confrontation.
key_facts: The narrator says that for weeks after returning from Baalum they had trouble remembering meetings, returning phone calls, and giving David an honest day's editing.
Sarah began sending for re-registration materials from Columbia once she snapped back into her old self.
Sarah seemed to have erased all memories of Baalum, except for occasional mumbles in Kekchi Maya.
Lou had not returned to work and mainly stayed at his Soho place to be near Sarah.
Steve returned to Belize to wrap up his photo essay.
David submitted a very rough cut of Baby Love to the selection committee at Sundance.
The hoped-for distribution deal with Orion was in temporary turnaround pending another management shuffle.
An advance from Lifetime lowered the heat with Nicky Russo.
The narrator's final dark dance with Alex Goddard, the man who thought he was Shiva, happened two months after they got back to the city.
The narrator was working late on a Thursday evening around seven o'clock in the editing room at Applecore.
The narrator had a headache and stomach pains from leftover pizza that had been microwaved.
The narrator was re-cutting new real-life interviews to replace those of Carly and Paula.
Children of Light had gone defunct and the phone at Quetzal Manor was disconnected.
The replacement interviews were less bubbly than the originals but truer to the realities of adoption.
